RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

An all-female panel is not evidence of bias. In the civil service, panel composition typically reflects internal availability and seniority rather than an intent to favor one gender. The successful candidate possesses strong, relevant qualifications, including international project leadership. 

Raising the panel's gender composition without concrete evidence of procedural irregularities or biased questioning will appear unprofessional and could harm your reputation within the civil service. Furthermore, a two-week turnaround for written feedback is standard in public administration. Instead of raising discrimination concerns, send a polite follow-up requesting your interview scores and constructive feedback to assist with future promotion opportunities.
